newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-COACH GETS LIFE BAN FOR ATTACK ON REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COACH GETS LIFE BAN FOR ATTACK ON REFEREE.

text.p: The head coach of Ukrainian premier division club Metalurg Mariupol was banned for life on Wednesday for beating up the referee and one of the linesmen who officiated over his side's home defeat on Sunday.
"Yuri Pohrebnyak was disqualified forever and will have no right to take part in any sporting event," league spokesman Valentyn Zaholuiko told Reuters.
The newly-promoted club were fined $5,000 and put on notice that the whole side will be thrown out of the championship if there is any more trouble. Pohrebnyak may also face prosecution.

Referee Vadym Shevchenko's nose was broken and he suffered rib fractures after Pohrebnyak allegedly led an angry gang of men who burst into his hotel room in the early hours of Monday after Mariupol went down 5-2 at home to Vorskla Poltava.

"I have not heard of anything like that since the days of the Soviet Union," Zaholuiko said. "The federation has decided not to disqualify the whole club. Why should players and the whole city suffer for a stupid act by one man?"
The southern club, sponsored by giant steel plant Azovstal, are bottom of the league after the first two games of the 1997-98 season. They lost 5-0 to Shakhtar Donetsk a week ago.
Rough treatment of match officials is a regular occurence in the former Soviet Union, though it normally happens in the heat of the moment on the pitch.
Russia's Rotor Volgograd were fined $2,000 on Wednesday after players badly roughed up the linesmen who ruled offside a last-minute equaliser in last week's top-of-the-table clash at Spartak Moscow.
